headline: PRESIDENT OF INDIA LAUNCHES BRAHMA KUMARIS’ CAMPAIGN ‘SPIRITUAL AWAKENING FOR WORLD RENEWAL’ AND INAUGURATES ‘GLOBAL SPIRITUAL PALACE’ RETREAT CENTRE AT VADODARA, GUJARAT
fullText:
President's Secretariat

PRESIDENT OF INDIA LAUNCHES BRAHMA KUMARIS’ CAMPAIGN ‘SPIRITUAL AWAKENING FOR WORLD RENEWAL’ AND INAUGURATES ‘GLOBAL SPIRITUAL PALACE’ RETREAT CENTRE AT VADODARA, GUJARAT

23 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu launched Brahma Kumaris’ campaign ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurated the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ Retreat Centre at Vadodara, Gujarat today (September 23, 2026). On the occasion, the President also virtually launched the campaign ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ of Brahma Kumaris Nadiad, Gujarat.

Addressing the gathering, the President said that today, there is a need not only for economic development but also for human development. We need an education that does not merely develop the intellect but also awakens wisdom. We need progress that is accompanied by sensitivity towards nature. We need a form of strength that teaches self-control rather than the control of others. We need spirituality that connects human beings. She was happy to note that the Brahma Kumaris organisation has spread the message of personal transformation and global renewal, through meditation and spiritual knowledge, not only across India but also to many countries around the world.

The President said that the potential for change exists within every human being. If people believe that changing their thoughts and actions can transform their life and if hope and self-respect are restored to them, they can become instruments of positive change not only for themselves but for society as a whole. She expressed confidence that today's inauguration of the Global Spiritual Palace will become a place where people from diverse sections of society can come together in peace and harmony.

The President said that it is heartening to virtually inaugurate the ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ campaign at Nadiad, the birthplace of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. She said that when the youth channel their thoughts, emotions, and actions in a positive direction, the impact extends to the family, the workplace, the community, and ultimately, the entire nation. Therefore, "Awakening Inner Strength" is not merely a message of personal development but a profound process of nation-building. She emphasised that it is our collective responsibility to empower the youth. We have to transform them into self-reliant, peace-loving and responsible citizens.

The President said that self-transformation is considered the foundation of societal transformation. Today, there is a need to align this great legacy with the requirements of modern life. Our goal should be to build an India that is economically prosperous, scientifically advanced, socially inclusive, and spiritually awakened.

headline: Day 2 of IIWW 2026 Brings Diverse Perspectives Together on Water Security, Innovation and Resilient WASH Services
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

Day 2 of IIWW 2026 Brings Diverse Perspectives Together on Water Security, Innovation and Resilient WASH Services

From Source Sustainability to AI-Enabled Solutions, IIWW 2026 Technical Sessions Spotlight the Future of Water Management

23 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW 2026) transitioned into its full technical schedule at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centering on the theme of climate-resilient water management. Organized by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the day featured parallel deliberations across Country, Water Leaders', Practitioners', and Thematic Forums, alongside dedicated side events and the concurrent Second International WASH Conference.

Addressing the Netherland-led Country Forum on “Success Stories in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability”, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena highlighted that India and the Netherlands share a common understanding that water management is not merely an engineering challenge but also a governance, community and climate-resilience challenge. He noted that India’s experience under Jal Jeevan Mission has demonstrated that water security requires strong political commitment, community ownership, scientific planning, accountable institutions and digital innovation working together. He further emphasised that the Mission’s focus is increasingly shifting from infrastructure creation to sustainability, service quality and long-term water security.

Shri Meena also highlighted the growing scope of India-Netherlands cooperation in advancing climate-resilient and sustainable water systems. He referred to initiatives such as the Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure and Decision Support Systems for source sustainability, which support data-driven planning, asset management and risk-informed decision-making. Emphasising the importance of source sustainability, greywater management and local government ownership, he noted that India looks forward to learning from the Netherlands’ extensive experience in water governance while deepening collaboration through research, innovation, capacity building and knowledge exchange.

The technical session on “Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas”, chaired by Ms Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary & Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), DDWS highlighted the increasing importance of greywater management in the context of expanding rural water supply coverage. The session brought together State Mission Directors, development partners, Panchayati Raj representatives and grassroots practitioners to share experiences and best practices from different parts of the country, including Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir and Jharkhand.

In her remarks, Ms Singh emphasised that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to greywater management and that solutions must be adapted to local conditions and community needs. The deliberations focused on decentralised treatment and reuse models, integration of greywater management into Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), and strengthening community participation to ensure sustainable water and sanitation outcomes in rural areas.

On the second day of the Second International WASH Conference 2026, six technical sessions were organised on the themes of (i) Digital Technology, AI and Innovation for WASH; (ii) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening; (iii) Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions and Sanitation; (iv) Water Quality, Safety and Emerging Contaminants; (v) Financing, Economic Models and Techno-Economic Solutions; and (vi) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening. A total of 25 technical papers were presented, showcasing innovative approaches, emerging research and practical solutions for strengthening climate-resilient and sustainable WASH services.

Technical sessions Details

The first technical session, “Digital Technology, AI & Innovation for WASH,” focused on the use of technology to strengthen the management, monitoring and maintenance of water and sanitation services. Four papers covered a digital communication and monitoring system for rural sanitation in Bihar, a low-cost IoT-based system for on-site detection of heavy metal ions, smart water meters as water-saving devices, and AI-driven decision support for predictive operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems. The presentations highlighted the potential of digital technologies, IoT and AI to improve service monitoring, efficiency and asset management.

The second technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, inclusive approaches and institutional collaboration for sustainable WASH services. Four papers covered a gender-inclusive sanitation model at PCMC, community ownership and digital engagement for rural piped water services in Bihar through the Dastak Abhiyan, inter-departmental collaboration for WASH through the Jal Vidya Programme in Assam, and a service-learning framework for rural sanitation. The session highlighted the role of community ownership, institutional coordination and inclusive approaches in strengthening WASH outcomes.

The third technical session, “Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions & Sanitation/Other,” focused on approaches to strengthening climate resilience and sustainability across water, sanitation and waste management systems. Four papers covered climate adaptation in urban water systems, a cost-effective climate-resilient model for solid waste management, participatory village planning for greywater management, and the application of remotely operated vehicles, AI and sensor technologies for water infrastructure protection and asset management. The session highlighted the role of climate-responsive planning, community participation and technology-enabled approaches in building resilient WASH systems.

The fourth technical session, “Water Quality, Safety & Emerging Contaminants,” focused on approaches to strengthening water quality management and water safety. Five papers examined an integrated approach to safe, energy-independent rural handpump water supply, drinking water quality under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Bongaigaon, Assam, sensor-based detection of water-borne pathogens, community-scale water disinfection technologies, and the use of Jal Jeevan Mission water quality data for seasonal public health risk identification. The presentations highlighted the importance of integrated monitoring, appropriate technologies and data-driven approaches to ensuring safe drinking water.

The fifth technical session, “Financing, Economic Models & Techno-Economic Solutions,” focused on approaches to improving the financial, technological and economic sustainability of WASH services. Four papers covered tablet-based inline chlorination as a cost-effective water safety solution, sustainable approaches to river water filtration and quality assessment, innovative economic models for rural WASH and community sustainability, and the socio-economic assessment of the GOBARdhan component in rural Gujarat. The session highlighted the role of cost-effective technologies, innovative economic models and local capacity building in supporting sustainable water and sanitation services.

The sixth technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, local governance and resilience in WASH service delivery. Four papers examined community participation and social governance in achieving SDG 6 in Rajasthan, the performance of the Swachh Bharat Mission in rural Hoshiarpur, Punjab, approaches to strengthening institutional linkages for flood-resilient WASH systems, and the climate resilience of rural water sources in PESA areas of Himachal Pradesh. The presentations highlighted the importance of community participation, institutional linkages, and locally responsive approaches in strengthening sustainable and climate-resilient WASH systems.

Discussion moved from the opening day's high-level themes into detailed, sector-specific work, spanning water governance and equity, technology adoption and efficiency, climate risk, treated wastewater reuse and community-led recharge. The Thematic Forum opened its paper presentations, across the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes. The sessions drew on the shortlisted papers gathered in the conference proceedings.

COUNTRY FORUM (CF)

CF-2 on Sharing Technology-Driven Initiatives in Water Security: German and EU Solutions for Sustainable Water Management in India, was chaired by Mr. Gottfried von Gemmingen, Head of Economic Cooperation & Development at the German Embassy in New Delhi, with GIZ, Siemens, Watershed Monitoring Inc., Asoti Engineering, HUBER Envirotech, and NIVUS Technologies, on digital and precision technologies for water security.

CF-3 on Success Stories of Countries in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability, convened with the Netherlands and CEEW was chaired by Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice-Minister of Water & Soil Affairs at the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, Govt. of the Netherlands and co-chaired by Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, IAS, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, discussed circular water economies, climate-resilient agriculture and knowledge transfer.

WATER LEADERS’ FORUM (WLF)

WLF-1 on Partnership and Cooperation for Inclusive Water Management, convened with Maharashtra and the World Bank, Drinking Water & Sanitation Department, Jharkhand; IWMI; Development Support Centre, Ahmedabad and Paani Foundation, Maharashtra, was chaired by Dr. Sanjay Belsare, Secretary (CAD), WRD, Maharashtra, and co-chaired by Shri Ajith Radhakrishnan, Senior Water Resources Management Specialist, World Bank, discussed partnership models for water access, quality and resilience across India's agro-climatic regions.

WLF-2 on Technological Solutions for Efficient Water Utilisation, convened with FICCI and chaired by Smt. Naina Lal Kidwai, Chair, FICCI Water Mission, FICCI and co-chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary & Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, focused on smart irrigation, digital water management, leak detection and industrial water efficiency.

PRACTITIONERS’ FORUM (PF)

PF-1 on State Initiatives in Water Management, was chaired by the Shri Bhopal Singh, Former Member, Central Water Commission, with Shri Zaigam Ali Khan Joint Secretary, NRCD as co-chair, brought together officers and representatives from WRD, Maharashtra; Greater Chennai Corporation; NEIDA; WRD, Madhya Pradesh; and WRD, Haryana, discussed State-level interventions in conservation and service delivery.

PF-2 on Large-Scale Adoption of Water Saving and Climate-Smart Technology: Lessons from States, was chaired by Shri Eknath Dawale, IAS, Principal Secretary, WRD, Maharashtra, and Shri Sumant Narain, Joint Secretary, National Water Mission as co-chair on micro-irrigation, solar pumps and digital mapping across Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka and Gujarat.

PF-3 on Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas, convened with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation was chaired by Smt. Aishvarya Singh, JS&MD, SBM(G), DDWS and co-chaired by Shri Brijesh Pandey, Secretary, PWD, Govt. of Tripura on the 3Rs (Reduce, Recharge and Reuse) approach, with about 5.46 lakh villages now having greywater management arrangements; the panel drew in SBM(G) mission directors and grassroots Swachhagrahis and sarpanches.

PF-4 on Smart Irrigation Management, was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), Central Water Commission, and co-chaired by Shri Rajeev Kumar, Chief Engineer, UGBO, Central Water Commission. The panelists discussed remote sensing, IoT and AI in irrigation, with IWMI and technology providers.

THEMATIC FORUM (TF)

Eight Thematic Forum sessions ran through the day presenting shortlisted papers and spanning the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes.

Sub-theme 1, Inclusive and Equitable Water Governance: TF-1 Equity in Water Allocation and Access to All Sectors, was chaired by Shri S. Masood Husain, Former Chairman, CWC, and co-chaired by Shri Vineet Gupta, Member, CWMA; TF-2 Water Governance Principles: Indicators, Audit and Standards, was chaired by Shri B. R. K. Pillai, Professor of Practice, IIT Roorkee, and co-chaired by Dr. P. Somasekhar Rao, Director (Technical), Advanced Centre for Integrated Water Resources Management, Govt. of Karnataka; and TF-3 Institutional Reforms and Strengthening was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), CWC with Shri Ashish Banerjee, Chief Engineer (IMO), CWC as co-chair. Papers examined equity-based groundwater allocation, women's participation in water governance and the Solar Didi self-help-group model, water auditing and benchmarking of irrigation projects, and parliamentary discourse on river governance.

Sub-theme 2, Collaboration for Optimal Use of Water Resources: TF-4 Treated Wastewater Reuse Across Sectors was chaired by Shri Praveen Gupta, Member (Thermal) Central Electrical Authority, with Shri Nalin Kumar Srivastava, Deputy Director General, NMCG as co-chair. TF-5 Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships for Efficient Water Management, was chaired by Shri S. K. Haldar, Chairperson, CWMA, with Shri Gopal Kumar, Country Representative, India & Bangladesh, IWMI as co-chair; and TF-6 International Collaboration in the Field of Climate-Related Risk chaired by Prof. Dr. Deepak Khare, Department of Water Resources Development & Management and co-chaired by Dr. Manish K. Nema, Scientist-E, National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee. Papers ranged over the circular economy in wastewater, water-sensitive cities, geospatial technologies in the Ken-Betwa link, and drought and flood risk assessment, including a basin-based approach to climate resilience in Kerala.

Sub-theme 3, Technology and Community for Water Security: TF-7 Forecasting and Modelling for Water Security, was chaired by Dr. A. K. Gosain, Professor Emeritus, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Delhi, and co-chaired by Dr. Ajai Pradhan, President & CEO, Cetus Consulting Pvt. Ltd. and TF-8 Community Participation in Groundwater Recharge, was chaired by Shri Cyril V. Darlong Diengdoh, Commissioner & Secretary, WRD, Govt. of Meghalaya and co-chaired by Dr. Dipankar Saha, Chair Professor, Center for Advanced Water Technology & Management, Manav Rachna University and Board President, Water for People. TF-7 spanned AI, machine learning and remote sensing for water security, SCADA and GIS integration, and flood modelling at river confluences; TF-8 drew on community-led desilting, spring rejuvenation, managed aquifer recharge and the Atal Bhujal Yojana.

SIDE EVENTS (SE)

SE-1 on Scaling Water-for-Food Solutions in India: Maximising the Impact of PMKSY through Finance, Partnerships and Innovation, convened by the World Bank with the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), examined how the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana can be strengthened through better financing, stronger partnerships and new innovation to make irrigation water go further for farmers. The session was chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary and Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, and graced by Shri Saroj Jha, Global Director, Water Department, World Bank, who brought a global perspective on financing water security for agriculture.

SE-2 on GSDP Conversation Series: Accelerating India's Water Vision 2047 through Indo-German Cooperation, convened by the German Embassy, looked at how the India-Germany partnership can help translate India's long-term water vision for 2047 into practical action on the ground.

H. E. Jasper Wieck, Ambassador, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, New Delhi, delivered the Inaugural Address. The session was also graced by the august presence of Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, who delivered the keynote address.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda to Inaugurate Arogya Manthan 2026, Tomorrow at Vigyan Bhawan
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda to Inaugurate Arogya Manthan 2026, Tomorrow at Vigyan Bhawan

Arogya Manthan 2026 to mark eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission

Arogya Manthan 2026 to Launch New Digital Health and Health Assurance Initiatives, Including Secure Data Environment (SDE) for Responsible Health Data Use

AB PM-JAY Covers Over 60 Crore Beneficiaries, Facilitates More Than 13 Crore Hospital Admissions Worth Over ₹2 Lakh Crore; Expansion to All Citizens Aged 70 Years and Above Extends Health Assurance to Around 6 Crore Additional Senior Citizens

ABDM Records Rapid Expansion with 97.8 Crore ABHAs, 121 Crore Linked Health Records and 11 Lakh Healthcare Professionals

24 SEP 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, will commemorate eight years of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) and five years of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) at Arogya Manthan 2026, being organised by the National Health Authority (NHA) tomorrow, at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.

The programme will feature a series of thematic deliberations focusing on key aspects of health assurance and digital health. The common session on “NHCX for Streamlining Health Insurance” will deliberate on the role of the National Health Claims Exchange in enabling standardised, streamlined and technology-driven health insurance processes.

This will be followed by parallel sessions under the AB PM-JAY and ABDM tracks covering “Claim Processing to Intelligent Assurance: Transforming AB PM-JAY”, with a focus on leveraging technology, data and analytics to strengthen claims processing and programme integrity; “Strategic Purchasing from the Perspective of Quality and Cost-Effectiveness”, examining approaches to improve quality of care and promote efficient utilisation of resources; “UHI for Improving Access of Healthcare Services”, focusing on leveraging digital platforms to expand access and participation across the healthcare ecosystem; and “Leveraging Standards for Better Health Delivery”, deliberating on the role of common health-data standards in enabling seamless exchange of information and strengthening continuity, efficiency and quality of healthcare delivery.

Aarogya Manthan 2026 will also witness the launch of a number of initiatives aimed at further strengthening India’s digital health and health assurance ecosystem. These include the National Healthcare Providers Registry (NHPR) Mobile App, NHCX Implementation Guide for Payers, Guidebook for a Model Digital Health Facility, Secure Data Environment (SDE) application and Framework for Auto-Adjudication of Claims under AB PM-JAY.

The Secure Data Environment, developed by NHA with the support of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, is envisaged as a governed environment for access to and analysis of AB PM-JAY and ABDM health data. Approved entities will be able to work with de-identified data or execute code within an isolated NHA environment, with outputs reviewed prior to release. The initiative is intended to facilitate health research, programme planning, outcome analysis and responsible AI innovation while incorporating safeguards for protection of personal data.

The event will also recognise best-performing States and Union Territories across various categories under AB PM-JAY and ABDM, acknowledging their efforts towards strengthening health assurance and digital health implementation.

About AB PMJAY and ABDM

Launched in 2018, AB PM-JAY has emerged as a key pillar of the Government’s efforts towards providing financial protection against hospitalisation to vulnerable families. The scheme provides health cover of up to Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Over the years, the scheme has expanded its reach across the country, with more than 60 crore beneficiaries covered under the scheme. It has also facilitated more than 13 crore hospital admissions, involving treatment worth over Rs. 2 lakh Crore.

A significant expansion of AB PM-JAY was undertaken in October 2024, when the scheme was extended to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status. The expansion has brought approximately 6 crore additional senior citizens within the ambit of the health assurance scheme.

Complementing the financial protection provided through AB PM-JAY, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), launched in September 2021, is creating the digital architecture for a connected, interoperable and citizen-centric health ecosystem. The Mission has established key digital health building blocks, including the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR) and Health Facility Registry (HFR), and has enabled a range of digital solutions to facilitate seamless access to healthcare services and exchange of health information.

As on September 1, 2026, more than 97.8 crore ABHAs have been created and over 121 crore health records have been linked. More than 5.6 lakh health facilities and 11 lakh healthcare professionals are registered on the ABDM ecosystem.

The Mission has also focused on developing digital health standards and enabling responsible use of technology and artificial intelligence in healthcare. Initiatives such as the Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India (SAHI), Benchmarking Open Data Platform in Health AI (BODH), Common Lab Codes for India and Bharat Health Terminology Service (BHTS) are contributing to the development of a standardised and interoperable digital health ecosystem. Citizen-centric initiatives such as Scan & Register, Scan & Pay and e-Sushrut Clinic are further supporting the adoption of digital health services.

Aarogya Manthan 2026 will bring together senior government officials, healthcare providers, insurers, technology and digital health experts, academia, development partners and other stakeholders to deliberate on the progress made under India’s health assurance and digital health programmes and discuss emerging priorities for the next phase. With eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM, Aarogya Manthan 2026 will provide an opportunity to take stock of the transformation underway in India’s health sector and deliberate on the priorities for the future.

headline: NHAI Guidelines to Strengthen Technology Integration and Sustainability in Development of High-Speed National Highway Corridors
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

NHAI Guidelines to Strengthen Technology Integration and Sustainability in Development of High-Speed National Highway Corridors

New guidelines focus on better planning, modern technology, smoother tolling, improved drainage and greener corridors

24 SEP 2026 4:27PM by PIB Delhi

Taking significant step towards developing a world-class National Highway network, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has released comprehensive guidelines for the planning and design of High-Speed Access-Controlled National Highways, other than Expressways. The new guidelines are aimed at ensuring that the High- speed National Highways are better designed & planned, safer, greener and ready to meet the needs of future traffic. The guidelines will apply to all upcoming four and six-lane Greenfield and Brownfield High-Speed Access-Controlled National Highways.

Data-Driven Planning for Future Traffic

The guidelines lay emphasis on comprehensive traffic assessment and future demand planning. Traffic projections shall take into account existing and diverted traffic, along with expected growth in freight movement linked to economic and commercial activities. Toll data and other reliable sources will also be used to make traffic estimates more accurate.

Technology-Enabled Construction

Use of modern technology will be enhanced during the construction of High-speed National Highways to improve quality, accuracy and monitoring. The guidelines provide for the use of Automated and Intelligent Machine-aided Construction (AI-MC) technology for construction of embankments and highway pavements, in accordance with applicable Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) guidelines. Incorporation of these measures will facilitate technology-enabled construction, enabling better quality, consistency and monitoring during National Highway development. Also as envisioned by the Government of India, a shift will be made to install Multi Lane Free Flow (MLFF) system of tolling on High-speed corridors, provisions for implementation of MLFF shall be made accordingly.

Landscaping and Environmental Measures from Planning Stage

Landscaping and plantation will be incorporated as an integral part of project planning. Landscaping and plantations will be planned at suitable locations such as loop areas, below flyovers, medians and other suitable locations, keeping in view local climate, topography and environmental conditions. Drip irrigation systems will also be provided on National Highway medians, to ensure efficient use of water and easier maintenance of plantations.

Better Drainage and Water Management

Comprehensive drainage planning will form an integral part of the DPR process. The planning will identify where rainwater will be disposed and how water from the National Highway and surrounding areas will be safely managed. Water harvesting structures will also be provided in loop areas and other suitable locations, particularly with no natural outlet for rainwater.

Special arrangements will be made to manage water around underpasses flyovers depressed medians and other structures, helping to prevent water logging and damage to the National Highway infrastructure. Drainage plans will clearly identify water disposal points and provide suitable arrangements for managing rainwater from the high-speed National Highways and surrounding areas.

The guidelines will significantly contribute towards development of safer, more sustainable and future-ready High Speed National Highway corridors across the country.

headline: 4th Edition of Bharat CPSEs’ Consultative Conclave Inaugurated at Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, Vadodara
fullText:

4th Edition of Bharat CPSEs’ Consultative Conclave Inaugurated at Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, Vadodara

Over 26 Senior Officers from 15 CPSEs of the Infrastructure, Transportation and Logistics Sectors, Subject Matter Experts from the academia and industry, Domain-Specific Faculty of GSV, Leading Industry Stalwarts, and Representatives of CBC and Union Ministries Converge on One Platform for Three-Day Consultative Deliberations on “Excellence in Project and Asset Management” under Mission Karmayogi

Conclave to Deliberate on PM Gati, ULIP, Multimodal Connectivity, Technology-Driven Asset Management and Global Best Practices, in Support of Viksit Bharat 2047

24 SEP 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Capacity Building Commission (CBC), Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, today inaugurated the 4th Edition of the Bharat CPSEs’ Consultative Conclave at the Sabhagriha Auditorium, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (GSV), Vadodara. Convened under the Mission Karmayogi framework, with GSV as the Strategic Knowledge Partner, the three-day Conclave (24–26 September 2026) has brought together, on a single consultative platform, over 26 senior officers from 15 Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) of the Infrastructure & Construction and Transportation, Logistics & Telecommunication Services sectors, along with subject matter experts from the industry and academia, domain-specific faculty members of GSV, associated industry stalwarts, and senior representatives of CBC and Union Ministries.

The Conclave’s thematic focus on Transportation, Logistics and Infrastructure sector assumes particular significance against the backdrop of the Prime Minister’s “Sapta Dhara” vision - the Seven Streams of Strength for Viksit Bharat, in his Independence Day 2026 address, in which Gati Shakti, denoting the creation of sustainable, world-class quality infrastructure, was identified as the fourth stream driving India’s development journey.

Inaugural Session

The Inaugural Session opened with a ceremonial lighting of the lamp by the dignitaries. Prof. Kaushik Das, Program Director from GSV and the CBC Task Force Member, presented an overview of the outcomes of Batch I of the Conclave and outlined the theme and objectives of the 4th Edition, followed by an inaugural address by Dr Alka Mittal, Member (Administration), CBC, and the context setting address by Prof. (Dr.) Manoj Choudhary, Hon’ble Vice Chancellor, GSV. This was followed by the Keynote Address of the Chief Guest of the event, Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI). The inaugural session concluded with a presentation on the findings of the pre-event diagnostic survey by Shri Sumeet Singh, Director, CBC. Dr. Nalin Shinghal, former CMD of BHEL and CEL, was welcomed by the Vice-Chancellor as the Program Mentor for the event.

A First-of-its-Kind Consultative Platform for Evidence-Based Governance

The Bharat CPSEs’ Consultative Conclave, conceptualised by CBC and supported by the Strategic Knowledge Partnership of GSV, given its extensive domain leadership in transportation, logistics and infrastructure, is the first initiative of its kind in India. By bringing public and private industry players, academic faculty and government officers together on one platform, the Conclave embodies a genuinely consultative model of capacity building, which is structured and designed keeping in view the practical challenges of project and asset management, as assessed directly from industry demand.

The knowledge briefs and documents emerging from the Conclave — culminating in the Bharat CPSE Compendium and an addressee-specific Reform Agenda — together with the extensive cross-learning generated among CPSEs, ministries, industry and academia, are expected to lend this institutionalised platform the stature of a thought-leadership - one that can guide and inform evidence-based decision-making, policy formulation and policy reform in India’s project and asset management ecosystem, in line with the vision articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

Three Days of Interactive, Participatory Capacity Building

Over the next two days, the Conclave moves into a series of thematic and breakout sessions structured entirely around industry-identified challenges in project and asset management — conceived as an interactive and participatory capacity-building exercise rather than a conventional lecture format.

The programme will conclude with an experiential learning field visit to the GSV Airbus Centre of Excellence, the Sardar Sarovar Dam and Statue of Unity at Kevadia, offering participants a first-hand view of large-scale infrastructure and project management in action.

“Kshamta SANGAM” Pre-Launch Joint Declaration: A New National Platform for Academia–Government-Industry Partnership all set for national launch in coming weeks

In a significant development during the Inaugural Session, CBC and GSV jointly declared to collaborate on its upcoming initiative - Kshamta SANGAM — Strategizing Atmanirbhar National Governance through Academia Mobilization. It will strategically leverage the collective knowledge resources and innovations of academia for futuristic capacity building and evidence-based governance in a systematic, scientific and outcome-oriented manner.

Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya today became the first academic institution to come on board this national mission, with the pre-launch Joint Declaration made by CBC and GSV, committing to take the initiative forward towards its official national launch in coming weeks under Mission Karmayogi.

fullText:

Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi to inaugurate Seva First Innovation Challenge at IISc Bengaluru

Will bring together young participants from five southern states and three union territories

Registration for the Event will be open from September 25 to October 24, 2026

24 SEP 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi will inaugurate the Seva First Innovation Challenge (SFIC), tomorrow, at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. The Initiative will encourage young people to identify problems they see in their communities and develop solutions that can be tested, improved and taken towards implementation. The Challenge will cover five states and three union territories including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Keralam, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Puducherry.

The Challenge will bring together young participants from schools, Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), polytechnics, colleges and universities. It has three levels of participation –Junior, Technical and Open. School students from class 6 to Class 12 can participate at the Junior level. At this level, students can identify local problems and develop simple working solutions or well-reasoned service and governance ideas. Students from ITIs and polytechnics will focus on hands-on engineering, fabrication, electronics and process solutions, while undergraduate students, postgraduates and research scholars will be expected to demonstrate prototypes or pilots with a credible pathway to deployment.

The Challenge will focus on five national themes, namely 1) Clean and Sustainable Bharat, 2) Prosperous Farmers, Prosperous Bharat, 3) Healthy and Inclusive Bharat, 4) Educated and Skilled Bharat and 5) Secure Bharat. Registration for the Event will be open from September 25 to October 24, 2026. It will culminate in the National Finale to be held in New Delhi from December 10 to 17, 2026.

Participants will have access to academic and industry mentorship, laboratories, fabrication facilities, testing support, incubation, seed and pilot funding, field-testing opportunities and guidance on intellectual property protection. Promising solutions can also be connected with Ministries, State Governments, urban and rural local bodies, public sector undertakings and industry for possible adoption.

The Challenge is being organised jointly by the Union Education Ministry, All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), University Grants Commission (UGC) with IISc Bengaluru serving as the nodal institute.

The initiative aims to foster a culture of community-rooted innovation, enabling young people to move from identifying problems to building solutions and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

For more details, please visit the official website: https://sevafirst.mic.gov.in/

headline: TDB-DST signs agreement with GalaxEye for ₹63.84 crore RDI support to develop next-generation multisensor satellite technology
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

TDB-DST signs agreement with GalaxEye for ₹63.84 crore RDI support to develop next-generation multisensor satellite technology

Indigenous OptoSAR technology to combine SAR and optical imaging for high-resolution Earth observation

24 SEP 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

Taking forward the Government of India’s push to accelerate private-sector research and development in strategic and emerging technologies, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s GalaxEye Space Solutions Private Limited, Bengaluru for financial support of ₹63.84 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

The project, with a total approved cost of ₹247.69 crore, is aimed at developing a multisensor satellite capable of high-resolution (<0.5 m) OptoSAR imaging and taking the technology from TRL-6 to TRL-9. The support will be extended through Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCD). At the heart of the GalaxEye project is OptoSAR, an approach that brings together two fundamentally different ways of observing the Earth — Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Electro-Optical (EO) imaging.

While optical imaging can provide highly detailed visual information, its effectiveness can be affected by cloud cover and illumination. SAR, on the other hand, can operate irrespective of daylight and can image through cloud cover. The proposed system seeks to bring these complementary capabilities together through fusion of SAR and EO data, enabling a richer and more continuous picture of the Earth.

The proposed satellite is designed to provide sub-0.5 metre high-resolution imaging. The technology is intended to support applications including wide-area and long-range surveillance, human and vehicle detection, and target classification, while enabling imaging across diverse weather and lighting conditions.

The project represents a significant technology-maturation programme, with the RDI support enabling GalaxEye to undertake further development, engineering, testing and validation required to progress the technology from TRL-6 to TRL-9.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “India’s space ecosystem is entering a phase where the ability to develop and deploy sophisticated technologies within the country will be increasingly important. The RDI Fund provides an important mechanism to support such technology-intensive efforts through the critical stages between advanced development and deployment. The agreement with GalaxEye reflects TDB’s focus on enabling indigenous capabilities in emerging space technologies and supporting their journey towards commercialisation.”

Promoters of GalaxEye Space Solutions Private Limited said,“The support from the Technology Development Board under the RDI Fund will enable us to accelerate the development and validation of our OptoSAR technology. By combining SAR and optical sensing, we are working towards an Earth-observation capability that can provide high-resolution information across a wider range of weather and lighting conditions. This partnership will be important in taking the technology towards TRL-9 and its subsequent deployment.”

headline: Indian Railways Approves ₹166.5 Crore for Construction of Road Over Bridge at Alkapuri in Vadodara Division
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Indian Railways Approves ₹166.5 Crore for Construction of Road Over Bridge at Alkapuri in Vadodara Division

Four-Lane Grade-Separated Road Facility to Augment Existing Alkapuri Road Connectivity and Address Traffic Constraints

24 SEP 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has approved the construction of a four-lane Road Over Bridge (ROB) at Alkapuri in Vadodara Division of Western Railway at a total cost of ₹166.5 crore, on a cost-sharing basis with the State Government.

The total project cost will be shared equally between Indian Railways and the State Government. The Railway share will be approximately ₹83.2769 crore, while the State Government share will also be approximately ₹83.2769 crore.

Four-Lane ROB to Augment Existing Road Connectivity

The existing Alkapuri Road Under Bridge (RUB) near Vadodara Railway Station serves as an important east-west road connectivity link between the Alkapuri and Kalaghoda areas of Vadodara city. However, the existing RUB has a vertical clearance of only about 3.0 metres, resulting in restrictions on the movement of larger vehicles and recurring waterlogging during the monsoon.

These limitations contribute to traffic congestion, operational difficulties and inconvenience for road users. The four-lane grade-separated road facility will augment the capacity and functionality of the existing road crossing arrangement.

Improved Connectivity to Key Transport Facilities

The ROB will provide an improved and more effective crossing facility without disturbing railway operations. It will also provide important connectivity to Vadodara Railway Station, GSRTC Bus Station and the upcoming High-Speed Rail (Bullet Train) Station.

Addressing Growing Traffic Requirements

The traffic assessment indicates peak-hour traffic of more than 1,600 PCU per hour, along with multiple traffic conflict points and inadequate pedestrian facilities. The existing RUB has consequently become inadequate to cater to the present and projected traffic requirements of the area.

The four-lane grade-separated facility will address the functional limitations of the existing RUB while augmenting road connectivity in this important part of Vadodara.

The project will strengthen the connectivity around Vadodara Railway Station while providing a more effective crossing arrangement and addressing the limitations of the existing Alkapuri RUB.

headline: Beyond one: Indian researchers’ experiment could lead to a new tool for quantum measurement
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Beyond one: Indian researchers’ experiment could lead to a new tool for quantum measurement

24 SEP 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi

Researchers have made the first experimental measurement of a quantum measure exceeding one, beyond the upper limit of ordinary probability. The result brings Quantum Measure Theory (QMT), a framework rooted in quantum foundations and the search for quantum gravity, into the laboratory, with potential applications in quantum measurement and computing.

Quantum mechanics is usually described in terms of the state of a system at a particular time and the outcomes obtained when we measure it. A complementary viewpoint is to describe a quantum system through its possible histories, meaning the different ways it can evolve between preparation and detection or the path that the photon could take in an experiment from a laser to a detector. QMT assigns a generalized measure to sets of such histories, incorporating the interference between them. Unlike an ordinary probability, this quantum measure can exceed one.

The difficulty is that a general set of histories does not necessarily correspond to a sequence of ordinary measurements, so its quantum measure is not straightforward to access experimentally.

An experiment by the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) has now measured the quantum measure assigned to a chosen collection of possible photon paths between the laser source and the detector.

In a future implementation, a filter could select a chosen collection of photon paths while leaving the photons available for further quantum operations. That could potentially turn this “event-filtering” into a new tool for quantum measurement and quantum computing.

To make QMT experimentally accessible, RRI physicists started constructing an “event-filter” that would select a set of photon routes (called event). Sanchari Chakraborti, then a PhD student at RRI, performed the experiment under the supervision of Urbasi Sinha, the paper’s co-author and senior professor at RRI.

To build this event-filter, they allowed the photons in the laser beam to traverse different routes in their optical setup. They then used polarisation, which tells the orientation in which the light waves are oscillating, to distinguish different routes and select the particular collection of routes they wanted. Later, they erased the distinguishing information so that the routes could interfere. In the reported experiment, published in the journal Quantum, the researchers measured input and output laser powers to infer the photon-detection probability. They then used the event-filter’s calibration to determine the “quantum measure”.

The quantum measure assigns a weight to a chosen collection of photon routes. They measured a quantum measure of about 1.17, agreeing within experimental uncertainty with the prediction of about 1.18 after accounting for imperfections in the apparatus. The value 1.17 showed that the quantum measure was behaving differently from ordinary classical probability that cannot exceed one.

Then how did the quantum measure exceed one? In the quantum world, contributions from different possible photon routes can also interfere with one another like waves: when two waves’ crests overlap, they create a bigger wave. This allows the quantum measure that includes interference between the routes to exceed one. The important caveat is that they didn’t measure a probability greater than one. The detector probability remains an ordinary probability below one. What can exceed one is the quantum measure.

Fig.: Event-filtering of quantum histories. An optical field explores multiple possible histories. The event filter selects a chosen set of histories while preserving the interference needed to determine their quantum measure. The measured result, μ(E)≅1.17, exceeds the classical probability bound of unity, even though the inferred photon-detection probability itself remains between zero and one. (Credit: Urbasi Sinha, RRI)

The study demonstrates for the first time the measurement of a quantum measure exceeding one. It shows that this quantity is not merely an abstract concept that can be calculated on paper: it can be measured experimentally. “There is something particularly satisfying about seeing an idea that grew out of fundamental questions about quantum mechanics become an optical experiment on a laboratory table. We’re not claiming that this resolves the quantum measurement problem,” says Sinha. “But we’ve enlarged the class of questions about quantum processes that can be connected to an experimental measurement.”

The quantum measure is central to QMT, which co-author Rafael Sorkin developed partly in the search for quantum gravity. Its focus on complete histories makes it a natural framework for describing quantum processes across spacetime. This experiment brings that framework into the laboratory; it does not test a theory of quantum gravity.

Sorkin, a researcher emeritus at Canada’s Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics and a Distinguished Visiting Faculty member at RRI, passed away on 12 September 2026, shortly after the paper was accepted.

“This paper means a great deal to me personally as well as scientifically,” says Sinha.

Publication Link: https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-09-24-2215

headline: Government Cuts Import Duty on Major Edible Oils to Provide Relief to Consumers
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

Government Cuts Import Duty on Major Edible Oils to Provide Relief to Consumers

BCD on Crude Sunflower Oil Cut to Nil; Soybean and Palm Oil Duty Reduced to 5%

19.25% Import Duty Differential between Crude and Refined Edible Oils maintained to support domestic refining

24 SEP 2026 12:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has reduced the Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on major imported crude edible oils with a view to moderating domestic edible oil prices, providing relief to consumers and mitigating inflationary pressures arising from the sharp increase in international edible oil prices.

Accordingly, the BCD on Crude Sunflower Oil has been reduced from 10% to Nil, while the BCD on Crude Soybean Oil and Crude Palm Oil has been reduced from 10% to 5%. The Government has simultaneously reduced the applicable BCD on the respective refined edible oils while maintaining an import duty differential of 19.25% between crude and refined edible oils.

The duty rationalization takes into account the increase in international edible oil prices and the consequent rise in domestic landed costs and retail prices. Import duties constitute an important component of the landed cost of imported edible oils and, therefore, have a bearing on domestic market prices.

The reduction in BCD on crude edible oils is expected to lower their landed cost and facilitate transmission of the benefit through the domestic supply chain. The measure is intended to provide relief to consumers while contributing to the broader objective of containing food-price and overall inflationary pressures.

The Government has maintained the duty differential between crude and refined edible oils to support the utilisation of domestic refining capacity and discourage excessive imports of refined edible oils. The measure is expected to provide a more level playing field for domestic refiners while supporting continued value addition within the country.

Advisory to Industry for Consumer Benefit

The Government has also issued an advisory to edible oil associations and industry stakeholders to ensure that the full benefit arising from the reduction in import duty is passed on to consumers.

Industry stakeholders have been requested to immediately revise their Price to Distributors (PTD) and Maximum Retail Price (MRP) in accordance with the reduction in landed costs. Edible oil associations have also been requested to advise their members to implement the corresponding price reductions without delay.

The Government will continue to monitor developments in international edible oil markets and domestic prices and will take appropriate measures, as necessary, to safeguard the interests of consumers while maintaining a balanced policy environment for farmers and the domestic edible oil industry.

headline: India Highlights Progress on Universal Health Coverage, Hepatitis Elimination and Sickle Cell Care at UNGA81
fullText:

India Highlights Progress on Universal Health Coverage, Hepatitis Elimination and Sickle Cell Care at UNGA81

India Showcases Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, AB-PMJAY and e-Sanjeevani in Advancing Universal Health Coverage at UNGA81

With Over 1.8 Lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, 900 Million+ Unique Health IDs and 497 Million+ Teleconsultations, India is Advancing Universal Health Coverage: Union Health Secretary

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlights Progress Towards Hepatitis Elimination by 2030 at UNGA81

India Joins Global Partners to Launch OneSCD at UNGA81, Advancing Equitable and Accessible Sickle Cell Care

India Highlights Comprehensive Sickle Cell Response and 2047 Elimination Goal at OneSCD Global Partnership Launch at UNGA81

24 SEP 2026 12:36PM by PIB Delhi

India reiterated its commitment to making quality healthcare accessible and affordable for all, while sharing its experience in strengthening public health systems and addressing priority health challenges at two key global health engagements held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA81) in New York.

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava participated in the Seventh Annual Ministerial Meeting of the Group of Friends of Universal Health Coverage (UHC) & Global Health, where she highlighted India’s efforts to strengthen healthcare delivery across the continuum, from comprehensive primary healthcare to secondary and tertiary care, while protecting people from financial hardship.

She highlighted India’s network of over 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, which bring a broad range of healthcare services closer to communities. These include services related to reproductive and child health, screening and management of non-communicable diseases, mental health, elderly and palliative care, along with preventive, promotive and curative healthcare. She also underlined the continued focus on quality standards in primary healthcare delivery.

Ms. Srivastava highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), the publicly funded health assurance scheme, in strengthening financial protection for vulnerable and underserved sections of society. She also underlined the importance of the Free Drugs and Diagnostics Service Initiative and the Prime Minister’s National Dialysis Programme in reducing the financial burden on patients and improving access to essential healthcare services.

Emphasising the importance of an integrated continuum of care, she noted that India’s approach connects comprehensive primary healthcare through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs with secondary and tertiary care, supported by referral linkages. The approach is aimed at bringing preventive, promotive and curative services closer to people while ensuring access to specialised care when required.

Highlighting India’s growing digital health ecosystem, the Union Health Secretary noted that over 900 million citizens have unique health identities. Interoperable digital registries of health facilities and healthcare professionals, along with ABHA-enabled health records, are helping strengthen continuity of care and facilitate access to health services.

She also highlighted the growing use of technology to bridge geographical barriers in healthcare. More than 497 million teleconsultations have been facilitated through e-Sanjeevani, alongside services and innovations such as teleradiology, AI-enabled X-rays and Mobile Medical Units. These initiatives are helping extend healthcare services to people in remote and underserved areas.

Delivering India’s perspective at the UNGA81 side event on “Advancing Global Action to Eliminate Hepatitis”, the Union Health Secretary highlighted the country’s commitment to the 2030 goal of eliminating Hepatitis B and C as public health threats. She underlined the importance of early diagnosis, affordable access to treatment and an integrated approach to prevention and care to accelerate progress towards this goal.

Embedded within the National Health Mission (NHM) framework, viral hepatitis screening services are being provided from nearly 1.80 lakh primary healthcare facilities, including Health and Wellness Centres, to tertiary care facilities. The programme has also expanded to 1,039 treatment centres. Since the launch of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme in 2018, nearly 225 million beneficiaries have been screened.

Ms. Srivastava also highlighted efforts to strengthen prevention by integrating viral hepatitis interventions across national health programmes, including measures to prevent mother-to-child transmission under the reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health framework.

She emphasised that sustained progress towards hepatitis elimination will require continued efforts to expand access, promote early diagnosis and ensure timely treatment, while strengthening health systems and integrating interventions across existing public health programmes.

At another key global health engagement on the sidelines of UNGA81, India co-hosted the launch of OneSCD: A Global Partnership to Advance Equity and Transform Sickle Cell Care, bringing together global partners to strengthen the international response to Sickle Cell Disease (SCD).

The initiative brought together partners including the Government of Nigeria, WHO, UNICEF, Africa CDC, the World Coalition on Sickle Cell Disease and St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital, with a shared focus on advancing more equitable and accessible approaches to Sickle Cell care.

Speaking at the launch, Ms. Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted India’s comprehensive response to Sickle Cell Disease through the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission, launched in 2023 under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, with the goal of eliminating Sickle Cell Anaemia as a public health problem by 2047.

She outlined India’s approach of integrating population-level screening, early diagnosis, counselling, treatment, follow-up and digital tracking into the public health system. The Mission seeks to identify the disease and carrier status early, facilitate appropriate counselling and ensure that individuals diagnosed with Sickle Cell Disease remain connected to care.

Under the Mission, more than 7.29 crore people have been screened, over 20 lakh carriers identified and 2.5 lakh people diagnosed, while more than 4.93 crore Sickle Cell Cards have been distributed. These efforts are helping strengthen the continuum of care and create greater awareness among individuals, families and communities about the disease.

The Union Health Secretary also highlighted efforts to expand access to affordable point-of-care diagnostics and hydroxyurea therapy, along with ongoing research towards an indigenous gene-editing therapy. She emphasised the importance of timely diagnosis, appropriate treatment and continued follow-up for people living with Sickle Cell Disease.

India’s participation in the two engagements reflects its continued efforts to strengthen health systems that are accessible to people across geographical and socio-economic settings. While the UHC discussions focused on building comprehensive, affordable and digitally enabled health services, the OneSCD initiative highlighted the importance of sustained global cooperation in addressing Sickle Cell Disease.

India reaffirmed its commitment to working with international partners towards equitable, affordable and people-centred healthcare, and to sharing experiences and approaches that can contribute to stronger health systems and better health outcomes globally.

PIB Backgrounder

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)

“When a Skill Opens Another Path”

24 SEP 2026 12:11PM by PIB Delhi

In villages where a family's future depends largely on harvests, acquiring a skill can often open up alternate livelihood pathways. For many rural youth, that path begins with an opportunity to learn, work, and build new sources of earning. That is where the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) enters the story. Launched on 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), DDU-GKY focuses on youth from marginalized and vulnerable rural households. It provides placement-linked skill training aimed at sustainable livelihoods. The programme targets youth aged 15 to 35 years, linking skill training with employment opportunities.

The programme is also changing with the world of work. The revised DDU-GKY 2.0 framework places greater emphasis on industry-led training, sustainable employment, post-placement support, upskilling and reskilling. An end-to-end digital system now covers training, assessment, certification, monitoring and employment tracking. It also strengthens employer engagement through partnerships, job fairs, campus placements and industry consultations.

The focus is clear: training should lead to work, and work should have a better chance of lasting. As of June 2026, 18.45 lakh rural youth have been trained under DDU-GKY, while 12.35 lakh have been placed.

Behind these numbers are stories of individuals whose lives changed when learning opened pathways to employment and livelihoods.

Keeping the Dream Alive

For years, Vimethano Sakhrie from Nagaland witnessed her mother work tirelessly to support a family of ten. After completing high school, Vimethano aspired to pursue higher education, but financial constraints made it difficult to realise that ambition.

Everything changed when she learnt about DDU-GKY. Refusing to give up on her dreams, she enrolled in a DDU-GKY tourism and hospitality training programme. Months later, Vimethano walked into her first job at The Den Bengaluru in Food & Beverage Service. It was more than employment. It marked the beginning of a new chapter for her and her family.

Looking back on her journey, Vimethano says, "I extend my gratitude to the Ministry of Rural Development and NSRLM, Government of Nagaland for implementing DDU-GKY, which has helped many unemployed youths across India. This opportunity was a blessing for me, and I hope many more youths can benefit from it, just like I did."

For Vimethano, DDU-GKY turned an interrupted education into a launchpad for a career. For Chandan Shah, the opportunity eventually led much further from home.

From Odd Jobs to a Career Abroad

There was a time when even basic necessities were difficult for Chandan Shah's family. Living in Tetahli village of Siwan, Bihar, he had little hope of continuing his education. He left school after high school to help his father in the fields. With few opportunities around him, Chandan took up odd jobs to earn a living. Yet, the work barely offered enough for a decent life.

A new possibility emerged through his mother, who was part of the Genda JEEViKA Self Help Group. She encouraged him to explore DDU-GKY. Chandan underwent counselling and chose to train as an Assistant Electrician. The training equipped him with the skills needed to take his first step towards a career. Upon completing the course, he secured his first job in Baddi as a helper at a distillery, earning ₹10,500 per month. This early experience provided him with a foundation for further professional growth. Building on these skills and experience, Chandan later pursued an opportunity overseas and moved to Dubai, where he joined Al Shafa General Contracting as an electrician.

By then, his monthly earnings had increased to ₹35,000. The impact extended beyond his own career, bringing greater financial security to his family. Chandan was able to support his family and contribute towards his siblings’ education in private schools. His journey also made him a source of inspiration for young people in his village.

Chandan’s story illustrates how a first employment opportunity can become a foundation for sustained livelihood progression. DDU-GKY equipped him with the skills to take that first step, while his determination and experience enabled him to pursue further opportunities. Together, they helped him build a more secure future for himself and his family.

Yet, not every DDU-GKY journey leads away from home. For Rupali Hasda, the opportunity eventually brought her back.

Turning a Job into an Enterprise

Financial hardship had forced Rupali Hasda of Charaideo, Assam, to leave school after Class 9. Her family depended on agriculture, with her father as the sole earner. Her mother, an active member of a Self-Help Group, continued to encourage her dreams. Rupali learnt about DDU-GKY through a Jeevika Sakhi and enrolled in the Sewing Machine Operator trade in December 2022.

After completing her training, she secured a job at KPR Apparels Mills in Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu. For five months, she worked in an unfamiliar city and adapted to a new environment. Yet, her thoughts remained close to home. She returned to Hatibandha with savings from her job and invested Rs.50,000 in a Sewing and Cutting Centre. What began as a livelihood for herself soon created an opportunity for someone else. She employed a young girl at the centre and began building an enterprise within her community. With an annual income of around Rs.1.10 lakh, Rupali's journey shows another side of skilling. A job gave her a start, but she chose to turn that experience into something of her own.

Rupali chose to build her livelihood close to home. Hiralal, however, sought a different path-one that would enable him to build a career while navigating the challenges before him.

A Career of His Own

Hiralal Pandit from Jharkhand had grown up watching every harvest decide how far his family's money would stretch. His family of four depended on his father's seasonal farming, which earned around Rs.5,000 a month.

After completing Class 10, he began helping his father in whatever ways he could. As a differently abled young man, finding work was far from easy. but Hiralal refused to let his circumstances define his future.

He aspired to build a career of his own while contributing to the financial well-being of his family. While exploring his options, Hiralal came to know about DDU-GKY. The programme’s free training and placement support offered him an opportunity to acquire skills and pursue employment. He enrolled in the Healthcare Multipurpose trade at a training centre in Dumka, Jharkhand.

The training marked a significant turning point in Hiralal’s journey. He acquired new skills in a supportive and inclusive learning environment where he was treated with dignity and equality. After completing the course, he secured placement at SMBT Hospital in Nashik as a General Duty Assistant. The opportunity enabled him to earn independently while contributing to his family’s well-being. More importantly, the experience strengthened his confidence and broadened his sense of what he could achieve.

Today, Hiralal encourages other young people to look beyond their circumstances and make the most of the opportunities available to them. For him, the journey began with the courage to take the first step. DDU-GKY helped him turn that first step into a pathway towards a career and a more secure future.

When a Skill Becomes a Livelihood

A skill cannot remove every hardship faced by a rural household, but it can open doors to greater possibilities. For Vimethano, it provided a route to employment when financial constraints interrupted her educations. For Chandan, it marked the beginning of a career that eventually took him to Dubai. Rupali brought her skills and experience back home to build an enterprise of her own, while Hiralal found an avenue to employment and an opportunity to support his family.

Their journeys took different directions, but they share a common thread: the chance to acquire skills, apply them, and build a livelihood. DDU-GKY seeks to make that first step possible, helping rural youth move from training to employment and from employment towards more secure and sustainable livelihoods.
