From Waste Picking to Greater Financial Security

Andhra Pradesh’s Chevuri Anjaneyulu’s Story

24 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

Assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE scheme has helped Shri Chevuri Anjaneyulu, a waste picker in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, earn additional income and improve his family’s financial security. He had spent seven years working to support his wife and two children.

A 25-year-old member of the Scheduled Tribe community, Mr. Anjaneyulu began accompanying his parents in waste-picking work at an early age. Financial hardship kept him from attending school. He has also faced social discrimination and lived with limited access to basic amenities and services.

Before the assistance, his income from waste picking made it difficult to meet household expenses and plan for his children’s future. He aspired to improve the family’s living conditions and provide his children with a good education.

On 19 June 2023, Shri Anjaneyulu and three other members received support for a group project under SUY through the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation. The total project cost was Rs 35 lakh, comprising a loan of Rs 17.5 lakh and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 17.5 lakh.

The assistance enabled him to strengthen his livelihood. He now earns approximately Rs 10,000 more per month through the scheme, helping the family meet its expenses more comfortably.

His two children are studying at an English-medium private school. The additional income has helped him support their education and work towards the better opportunities he had long hoped to provide.

For Shri Anjaneyulu, this support has meant greater economic stability and a more secure future for his family. His experience shows how access to livelihood assistance can help waste pickers improve their income and pursue their aspirations.

headline: Keralam’s Cultural Mementos Up for Auction at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Keralam’s Cultural Mementos Up for Auction at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026

A collection spanning traditional crafts, performing arts, maritime traditions and spiritual heritage

24 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

A diverse selection of 32 mementos from Keralam is being offered at the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, bringing together the state’s art, craftsmanship, performing traditions and cultural heritage. The collection features distinctive pieces ranging from a traditional Nettoor Petti and a miniature Chundan Vallam to Kathakali and Theyyam artefacts, Keralam mural art and a handcrafted model of the historic Beypore Uru.

The Orange Nettoor Petti - Keralam Traditional Jewel Box with Mural Art and Brass Detailing describes the Nettoor Petti as having been historically used in aristocratic households to store ornaments and sacred objects, reflecting the traditional craftsmanship associated with this form.

Keralam’s maritime traditions find representation in a finely crafted Chundan Vallam, the traditional snake boat associated with the state’s backwaters and the boat races of the Onam festival. Another notable piece is a miniature Beypore Uru, a traditional wooden maritime dhow. The model was handcrafted by the National Skill Training Institute (NSTI), Calicut, under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and replicates the wooden dhows traditionally built by master carpenters of Beypore.

The collection features several representations of Keralam’s performing arts. A Kathakali dancer display doll and a print of a Kathakali performer depict elements of the classical dance-drama, including its elaborate makeup, costumes, ornaments and headgear.

Another distinctive piece is the Bhairavan Theyyam Ritual Art Sculpture, representing Bhairavan Theyyam, described in the collection as an iconic manifestation of Lord Shiva from the ritualistic dance-art tradition of North Keralam. The sculpture features the characteristic headgear, facial makeup, breastplates and traditional attire associated with the form.

Kerala’s mural tradition is represented by a framed painting of Radha, Krishna and a Gopika, created by artists at the Institute of Mural Painting, Guruvayur Devaswom. The artwork depicts Lord Krishna playing the flute beneath a banyan tree, with Radha and a Gopika and is executed on a specially prepared cement sheet using the traditional five-colour Panchavarna formula.

The collection also includes works associated with Kerala’s spiritual and social heritage. These include a devotional portrait of Adi Shankaracharya, a carved wooden plaque featuring Sivagiri Mutt Commemorative Carved Wooden Temple, a framed print of Poykayil Sree Kumara Gurudevan and a framed photograph of Sree Vidyadhiraja Chattambi Swamikal.

A framed commemorative artwork marking 100 Years of Vaikom Satyagraha is also part of the collection. Other pieces include a traditional Nettipattam, a Kerala brass Vastu Vilakku, a carved wooden statue of Lord Guruvayurappan, a traditional Shankhu (conch) memento and many more.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, live until 2 October 2026, brings together mementos representing Kerala’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: pmmementos.gov.in

headline: Sowa Rigpa Has Significant Potential in Education, Research and Healthcare: Ayush Secretary, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha
fullText:
Sowa Rigpa Has Significant Potential in Education, Research and Healthcare: Ayush Secretary, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha

Three-Day National Workshop in Leh Explores Opportunities and Challenges for Sowa Rigpa in Post-Recognition Era

24 SEP 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, has called for greater focus on education, research, healthcare, documentation and standardisation to further strengthen Sowa Rigpa and expand its recognition at the national and international levels.

He was addressing the valedictory function of the three-day National Workshop on the “Scope and Challenges of Sowa Rigpa Post-Recognition”, organised by the National Institute of Sowa Rigpa (NISR), Leh, at the New Academic Building, Saboo Thang, Leh.

Highlighting the growing scope and global relevance of traditional systems of medicine, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha said that Sowa Rigpa has significant opportunities in education, research, healthcare, documentation and standardisation. He also emphasised the importance of wider recognition of the system at the national and international levels.

Encouraging students and young scholars of Sowa Rigpa, the Secretary urged them to approach emerging challenges with confidence, dedication and innovation. He encouraged them to “keep the sky as the limit” and explore new possibilities that can contribute to the advancement of Sowa Rigpa.

The workshop brought together experts, scholars, practitioners, administrators, students and other stakeholders from different parts of the Himalayan region to deliberate on the evolving scope, opportunities and challenges of Sowa Rigpa following its recognition as a system of medicine.

The technical sessions focused on institutional development, education, research, healthcare practices, preservation of traditional knowledge, standardisation, and emerging opportunities and challenges in the post-recognition era. The deliberations provided a platform for interaction and exchange of ideas among stakeholders and contributed to strengthening the academic, professional and institutional framework of Sowa Rigpa.

The programme was also organised as part of the National Ayurveda Day celebrations, providing an opportunity to highlight the rich heritage and contemporary relevance of India’s diverse traditional systems of medicine.

Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director, National Institute of Sowa Rigpa, welcomed Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha and expressed gratitude for his continued support towards the preservation and promotion of Sowa Rigpa.

Dr. Tenzin Kunphel, Chairman, Central Council of Tibetan Medicine (CCTM), Dharamsala; Dr. Dorje Damdul, Associate Professor and Dean, Faculty of Sowa Rigpa and Bhot Jyotish, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sarnath, Varanasi; and Dr. Phunsok Wangchuk, former Director, Health and Ayush, UT Ladakh, were among the distinguished dignitaries present on the occasion.

The dignitaries shared their experiences and perspectives on the development of Sowa Rigpa and its academic and research potential.

Following the valedictory function, participants visited the Trans-Himalayan Herbal Garden at Phey. They observed various medicinal plants cultivated and conserved in the garden, gaining practical exposure to the rich medicinal plant diversity of the Trans-Himalayan region. The visit complemented the academic deliberations of the workshop.

Ministry of Jal Shakti

IIWW 2026: India and Netherlands Strengthen Strategic Partnership in Water Sector

Two MoUs Signed for Technical Cooperation and Capacity Building on Kalpasar Project

24 SEP 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil and Vice Minister for Infrastructure and Water Management, Netherlands, H.E. Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, chaired a bilateral meeting between India and the Netherlands on the Strategic Partnership on Water at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on the sidelines of the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026.

Minister of State for Jal Shakti Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Minister of State for Water Resources and Water Supply (Independent Charge), Government of Gujarat, Shri Ishwarsinh Patel, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation Smt. Archana Varma, Chairman, Central Water Commission Shri Anupam Prasad, Ambassador of the Netherlands H.E. Ms. Marisa Gerards and other senior officials were also present.

The meeting provided an opportunity to review and further strengthen India–Netherlands cooperation in the water sector with particular focus on advancing technical cooperation for the Kalpasar Project in Gujarat. As part of the bilateral engagement, two Tripartite Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) were signed to facilitate cooperation for the Kalpasar Project between the Central Water Commission (CWC), Kalpasar Department, Government of Gujarat, and Dutch knowledge institutions Deltares and TU Delft.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C R Patil said that he was pleased to see Deltares and TU Delft entering into MoUs with their Indian counterparts to deepen cooperation in the execution of the Kalpasar Project and capacity building. He expressed confidence that the MoUs would provide a strong basis for both countries to work together towards the successful execution of the project.

The Minister noted that the Kalpasar Project was discussed during Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s visit to the Netherlands in May 2026, following which a Letter of Intent for technical cooperation was signed on 16 May 2026. He said that the project envisages creation of a freshwater reservoir using runoff from the Sabarmati, Mahi and Dhadhar rivers, supplemented by water conveyed from the Narmada River.

He further highlighted that during the Indian delegation’s visit to the Netherlands in July 2026, valuable insights were received in areas including flood protection, coastal infrastructure, hydraulic modelling, sluice and pumping systems, dyke technologies and ecological solutions. He noted that there were useful parallels with the Afsluitdijk in the Netherlands, particularly in terms of engineering, water management and coastal infrastructure.

Vice Minister for Infrastructure and Water Management of the Netherlands, H.E. Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, highlighted the importance of the Letter of Intent for technical cooperation on the Kalpasar Project and the opportunities it presents for further India–Netherlands cooperation. Referring to the Afsluitdijk, he said that the structure is nearly 100 years old and is now being renewed, providing an opportunity for the Netherlands to share the experience and knowledge accumulated over the past century. He added that Dutch institutions such as Deltares and TU Delft would contribute their expertise through the MoUs, providing a foundation for further collaboration in the water sector. He also emphasised the importance of sharing lessons learned, particularly in areas such as ecology and fish migration.

The MoUs will facilitate technical collaboration through sharing of Dutch expertise and advanced engineering practices for the planning, design and implementation of the project. The cooperation with Deltares, inter alia, covers technical review, hydraulic and hydrological modelling, coastal and structural engineering, climate resilience, capacity building, knowledge transfer and digital applications.
